stem:
Yash measures a ribbon using the fractional unit $\dfrac{1}{8}$ metre. Exactly $5$ of those units cover the ribbon end to end.

Which claim correctly writes the ribbon length?

options.text: The length is $5$ metres, taking only the count of units.
Say that writing $\dfrac{5}{8}$ is what creates the unit size $\dfrac{1}{8}$.
The length is $\dfrac{5}{8}$ metre, because $5$ copies of $\dfrac{1}{8}$ make $\dfrac{5}{8}$.
The same reading $\dfrac{5}{8}$ also fixes the length when a different unit such as $\dfrac{1}{10}$ is chosen instead.

teacher.key_rationale: n copies of unit 1/d make length n/d, so 5 copies of 1/8 make 5/8 metre. Dropping the unit size, reversing length as what creates the unit, or carrying the reading to a different unit all miss that count.
